sections.h2: What sets High Point, NC apart for a home seller?
sections.html:
High Point bills itself as the Home Furnishings Capital of the World, and the city's tourism site says it hosts the High Point Market, a wholesale home furnishings show held each spring and fall and open to retailers and design professionals. The same site mentions the World's Largest Chest of Drawers and Furnitureland South, a store with more than a million square feet of showroom space.

An older city financial report says the corporate limits touch four counties. The bulk of the city lies in southwestern Guilford County, and roughly two percent of its area spills into Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth. That detail decides which tax office, register of deeds and appeal board handle your parcel, so check the county named on your deed.

  • An agent listing reaches buyers across the Triad region.
  • A private sale fits when you already have a buyer.
  • A cash buyer suits a house in poor repair or a short fuse on the calendar.

sections.h2: How does the furniture industry shape the High Point housing picture?
sections.html:
The city's older annual report describes the home furnishings cluster as a major employer. It cites a study putting the annual economic impact of the market on the four county Triad region (Davidson, Forsyth, Guilford and Randolph) at $8.25 billion and more than 69,000 local jobs tied to manufacturers, corporate offices, distribution centers, design centers, showrooms and suppliers. Those figures come from a report of some age, so treat them as background rather than current numbers.

For a seller, the point is that demand for housing here connects to an industry with seasonal peaks. The tourism site notes the two market sessions each year, and short-stay housing needs during those weeks are part of local life. If you consider a rental after buying or inheriting a house, ask the city planning office about its rules before you advertise. Home occupations, for example, require a zoning permit under the city's permits page.

sections.h2: Do permits matter when you sell a High Point house?
sections.html:
Yes. The North Carolina Building Code requires a permit before building, repairing or altering a structure, and High Point's Development Ordinance adds a zoning permit for activities outside the building code. The city's permit specialists answer questions at 336-883-3151.

The city lists typical zoning permit projects, including signs, fences, accessory buildings with every dimension at 12 feet or less, and home occupations. Permits are filed online through Accela Citizen Access, and the permit holder must schedule each inspection. A final inspection produces a certificate stating the project complies with code.

Before listing, confirm three things with the permit office: whether any open permit exists on the address, whether past additions received final inspections, and whether a fence or accessory building you built falls under the zoning permit list. Each one is easier to settle with the seller in control than in the middle of a buyer's inspection period. Copies of permit applications are posted in PDF form, which shows exactly what the city required for each type of project.

Permits do expire: a construction permit lapses six months after issuance if work has not started, and also when work is abandoned for 12 months. A zoning permit lapses after six months if work has not begun. An unfinished old project should be sorted out early, before a buyer's inspector spots it.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 Guilford County reappraisal affect High Point homes?
sections.html:
Most High Point parcels sit in Guilford County, which made new values effective January 1, 2026. Owners were to be notified in February 2026, and the new values flow to the bill the county sends in July 2026. The deadline to appeal was 5 p.m. on May 15, 2026, so that window has closed.

The county did the appraisal in house, drawing on maps, aerial photos, street-level images, sales analysis and field visits. Vehicles and boats are outside it because their values are adjusted every year. The state revenue department had required the 2026 reappraisal in April 2023.

The county's appraisal line is 336-641-4814. If your parcel lies in the Randolph, Davidson or Forsyth portion, ask that county's assessor how its cycle works.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 Guilford reappraisal timeline look like?
sections.html:
The county lays its schedule out in plain dates, and every one of them is now in the past except the effects that carry into later bills.

Guilford County 2026 reappraisal milestones as published by the county
MilestoneDate
New values effectiveJanuary 1, 2026
Owner noticesFebruary 2026
Values appear on the billJuly 2026
Rates set by elected officialsJune 2026, for the year ending June 30, 2027
Appeal deadline5 p.m., May 15, 2026

Source: Guilford County 2026 reappraisal. Later disputes go first to the review board that the commissioners sit as, then to the state Property Tax Commission, each under written deadlines in G.S. 105-322 and 105-290. Useful evidence listed by the county includes comparable sales, a recent appraisal, property card errors and outside factors such as flood zone.

sections.h2: Which tax breaks might follow a High Point owner?
sections.html:
Three state programs exist, and an owner can use only one. A disabled veteran exclusion has no age or income limit, while the elderly or disabled exclusion and the circuit breaker are tied to an income cap that the 2026 state form prints as $38,800.

Apply on Form AV-9 with the county assessor. Ask the county for a payoff before closing if the circuit breaker deferred any tax, because that deferred amount is a lien that falls due on a transfer.

sections.h2: What problems can complicate a High Point sale?
sections.html:
Three come up often: an unpaid tax lien, owner financing on a handshake, and a long-term occupant with no lease.

  • Tax lien: it attaches as of the listing date, and the county can foreclose through a court action modeled on a mortgage foreclosure. The sale is by auction at the courthouse door, and the owner may redeem before confirmation by paying taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
  • Contract for deed: Chapter 47H gives the buyer until midnight of the third business day to cancel, and a forfeiture needs written notice with a cure date at least 30 days out.
  • Occupant: possession under known and visible lines for 20 years can bar the owner's claim, so address a long-time occupant of a vacant parcel promptly.

A title search before you list uncovers these issues while there is still time to fix them.

faqs.q: Which county handles my High Point property taxes?
faqs.a: Look at the county on your deed. Most of High Point lies in Guilford County, while about two percent of the city's area reaches Randolph, Davidson and Forsyth counties, each with its own assessor.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Guilford value appeal still available?
faqs.a: No. The deadline was May 15, 2026 at 5 p.m., and the county lists the period as closed. Later disputes begin with the review board and can reach the state Property Tax Commission.

faqs.q: What building permit phone number does High Point list?
faqs.a: The city's permit specialists are reachable at 336-883-3151, per the Permits Required page. Permit applications are filed online through Accela Citizen Access, and copies of every application form are posted as PDFs so you can see the submittal requirements first.

faqs.q: How long does a High Point construction permit last?
faqs.a: It expires six months after issuance if work has not begun, and also if work stops for 12 months. Zoning permits under the city's ordinance expire after six months without a start. Once a project is complete, a final inspection leads to a certificate that the work is code compliant.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property tax lead to a forced sale in High Point?
faqs.a: Yes, through a county foreclosure action and an auction. The owner may redeem before confirmation by paying all taxes, penalties, interest and costs.
